[[File:Mike Patterson and Tom Hoge 2015.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Tom Hoge and Mike Patterson, November 2015.<ref name="ars" />]]
'''Mike Patterson''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Red 94 from Houston, Tx. His slot was marked Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.<ref name="sm-fan" /> In November 2015 he joined [[Eric Berger]] and Tom Hoge, fellow former players, for a sealed-deck mini tournament.<ref name="ars">[https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ That one time I played in the Star Wars card game world championship], Eric Berger, Ars Technica (5 December 2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009010838/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support).

== Jedi Knights TCG ==

Patterson playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref>
